title: Typography and Spacing Systems knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Typography and Spacing Systems” in Dart Sass?
options: The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

Values become easier to maintain when their role and lifetime are clear. Sass variables are resolved during compilation; CSS custom properties remain in emitted CSS and can change at runtime through the cascade.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
questions.answer_key: Values become easier to maintain when their role and lifetime are clear. Sass variables are resolved during compilation; CSS custom properties remain in emitted CSS and can change at runtime through the cascade.
questions.explanation: Values become easier to maintain when their role and lifetime are clear. Sass variables are resolved during compilation; CSS custom properties remain in emitted CSS and can change at runtime through the cascade. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Font families and fallbacks”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: For font families and fallbacks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
questions.answer_key: For font families and fallbacks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.explanation: For font families and fallbacks, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Typography and Spacing Systems”?
options: Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

Name values by purpose, group related tokens, and provide sensible defaults only when consumers are meant to configure the system. Test valid and missing keys, incompatible units, and the actual rendered contrast or layout.
questions.answer_key: Name values by purpose, group related tokens, and provide sensible defaults only when consumers are meant to configure the system. Test valid and missing keys, incompatible units, and the actual rendered contrast or layout.
questions.explanation: Name values by purpose, group related tokens, and provide sensible defaults only when consumers are meant to configure the system. Test valid and missing keys, incompatible units, and the actual rendered contrast or layout. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
